title: California gas prices could drop up to 30 cents with winter-blend switch
excerpt: The statewide average hit $6.08 a gallon this week, but analysts say the late-October switch to winter-blend fuel could shave 10 to 30 cents off each gallon.
body:
• California's average gas price hit $6.08 a gallon on Thursday, up 19 cents in a single week, according to AAA.
  • Drivers may get relief by late October, when the state switches to cheaper winter-blend gasoline — a change analysts say could shave 10 to 30 cents off each gallon.
  • Diesel has reached a record $8.35 a gallon, up $3.18 over the past year, threatening to push up the cost of everyday goods.
  • Analysts warn prices could climb further before the blend switch, with Middle East tensions and the Strait of Hormuz crisis keeping crude markets on edge.

California drivers may finally catch a break at the pump next month. After weeks of punishing price hikes pushed the statewide average above $6 a gallon, analysts say the annual switch from summer-blend to winter-blend gasoline — due by the end of October — could cut prices by 10 to 30 cents a gallon, offering the first real relief in a brutal year for motorists.

Prices jumped 19 cents in the past week alone, bringing the statewide average for a gallon of regular to $6.08 as of Thursday, according to AAA. The pain has been even sharper in parts of the Bay Area, where prices climbed 20 cents in San Jose and 21 cents in San Francisco over the same seven-day stretch, KRON4 reported. Solano County was the only Bay Area county still below the statewide average, with regular averaging $6.03 a gallon.

Context & Background

The summer-blend gasoline California mandates during warmer months costs more to refine, which is why the state's prices reliably ease each fall. But this year's spike has been driven by something bigger than seasonal blends. The war between the United States, Israel and Iran — which began Feb. 28 and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — has jolted global energy markets, pushing crude oil into the $90-a-barrel range, AAA said. Continued volatility around Hormuz has kept California's prices among the highest in the nation.

Over the past year, the statewide average has surged $1.43 a gallon. Diesel has been hit even harder: it now averages a record $8.35 a gallon, up $3.18 from a year ago. Analysts note that diesel powers the trucks that move goods across the state, so record diesel prices can ripple into higher prices for groceries and everyday items as transport costs work through the supply chain.

Impact & Analysis

The fall blend switch is a genuine, mechanical reprieve — winter-blend fuel is cheaper to produce, and the switch historically trims California prices. Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, told the New York Post the seasonal change could knock 10 to 30 cents off the per-gallon price.

But the relief is neither guaranteed nor lasting. De Haan cautioned that prices could keep climbing before the switch, with much depending on developments in the Middle East and around the Strait of Hormuz. And even a 30-cent drop would leave California drivers paying close to $5.80 a gallon — far above the national average of $4.14, which AAA says has never been above $4 on Labor Day before.

Diaspora Angle

For the Bay Area's large Indian diaspora community — concentrated in San Jose, Fremont, Sunnyvale and Santa Clara, some of the priciest pump territory in the state — the relief could not come sooner. Many families face long commutes along the 101 and 880 corridors, and with the holiday season approaching, the expected October dip could make Diwali and Thanksgiving travel noticeably cheaper than filling up this week.

What's Next

Watch the blend transition in the final week of October, when refiners complete the switch and stations begin selling winter gasoline. If crude markets stay calm and Hormuz tensions ease, drivers could see steady declines into the holidays — a pattern that historically trims prices about 10 percent between September and year-end. If Middle East tensions escalate, expect the current $6-plus regime to persist into 2027.
